commits.message:
fix(click): the host and every renderer hold the one key the daemon read, and every click writes its event (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.35o)

- One reader of the link key feeds the host's signer and each renderer's
  boot, so a key file removed and made again while the daemon runs can no
  longer leave the two on different keys, refusing every click.
- Whatever a click throws becomes its outcome where every click is run, so a
  status-line click whose opener fails writes its event and answers its
  failure.
- A URL frame the daemon could not handle (it is closing) is answered with the
  failure instead of leaving the app to wait out its timeout.
- The app tells a frame written but answered with no verdict as "Click
  unconfirmed", since the click may still land.
- A non-bar link's own #fragment stays in the click's event.

fix(click): the host opens every link's signature before a renderer sees it, and tells the app its verdict at once (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.35o)

Every link the bar draws is signed once per draw, and the host opens the
signature before parsing: a forged, edited or unsigned link reaches no
renderer, and its sender is told why.

- A v2 URL frame is answered with its verdict as soon as it is read, and the
  click runs after it under the deadline: a slow click that lands is never
  told as failed. The app shows "Click refused" with the host's reason, or
  "Click not delivered". A v1 writer hangs up as before.
- The link key is read where it is used: the host's signer is lazy and
  retries, and each renderer start reads it afresh into its boot. A broken
  key refuses the start on ⚠; removing the file recovers at the next start.
- A doctor probe is the host's own arm of the click reading, so it arrives
  whatever state the key is in. The renderer's probe verb is gone.
- check, the demo, the bench and the doctor's config draw sign with a random
  preview key, so they never create the key file.
- The page's memfs volume takes its owner from the page's process, so a file
  only its owner may open (the link key) opens.

feat(renderer): the renderer runs in a process of its own, which the host's supervisor starts and restarts (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.v58) (#757)

* feat(renderer): the renderer runs in a process of its own, which the host's supervisor starts and restarts (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.v58)

The daemon's process runs its main renderer as a child, speaking the
renderer interface as JSON lines over its stdio; tests, the page and
`check` keep the in-process transport over the same Renderer and
AdapterToHost.

- The supervisor owns the child's life as one state: it starts one as the
  daemon arms, queues inputs while it boots, fails inputs at once as `down`
  while none is live (counted, said once at the next start), and restarts
  one that ended after a backoff that doubles while renderers end young.
- A start is complete: a `config` for every live session whose newest
  request the host holds, and a `pin` for every open feed. An ended
  renderer's watches and storage holds stay held until the next has
  answered its start.
- Ids a renderer mints for effects, watches and storage holds cross as the
  host's own, never repeated across renderers.
- A ping every ten seconds, answered outside any turn, ends a renderer that
  stops answering for a minute, and carries its memory.
- The memory backstop charges the host and its renderer together (one
  footprint call over both pids on macOS, the RSS sum on Linux). A breach
  writes each process's attribution and both heap snapshots, and the
  doctor and daemon-stats report each process's share.
- How the last renderer ended is a held event on the daemon's facts, which
  every bar shows as a `⚠` by the pipe event's hold; the adapter's answer
  notice is now `eventAnswered`, for every daemon-wide held event.
- The update notice's dismiss gate moves to the renderer, following the
  newest answered update fact its world states carry.
- The request event reports the hop's cost beside `took`.
- A feed whose frame step keeps throwing one fault says it once, and says
  its recovery.

Spec §8 and §9 are amended to match.

* fix(renderer): a restart's start heads the boot's queue, a refused boot says why, and the renderer launches through the daemon's own launcher (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.v58)

The restart's config and pin are queued at spawn, ahead of every input that
arrives during the boot, so none repeats or contradicts them; its turns are
recorded through deliver. A close during a boot fails what waited for it. A
gone renderer's holds stay until a start answers. A refused boot's reason
reaches the bar's warning. A booting renderer counts in the memory charge,
and the breach's renderer snapshot targets the measured process only and
rechecks the close after it. The boot carries the host's source digest in
place of a hand-bumped protocol number. A call line reaches the host as it
arrives. A channel ends only once its pipes have closed. The daemon event
hold is one constant. The update gate follows an equal-stamp fact. A feed
recovers only after a whole step. The doctor names build skew under a
reading it cannot parse.

* fix(renderer): a gone renderer's holds go only once the next has started and taken its start; the renderer keeps the process's launcher (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.v58)

The start runs at spawn, so one with nothing to await released the old
renderer's watches before the new one booted; the release now waits for
both. A second launcher for the renderer doubled every lifeline warning and
put a launcher into every in-process daemon, for faults the renderer's end
already reports, so the renderer runs under the process's launcher again. A
channel's end waiting for its pipes could hang a restart and the close on a
descendant holding them, so it resolves on the child's end, and its contract
says a last line may follow. An input naming an ended renderer's effect or
watch fails as its own logged failure rather than as an uncounted down. A
feed closed while it drew logs no recovery.

* fix(renderer): a boot that never answered counts young, only a renderer that took over hands its holds on, and a line after its end reaches nothing (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.v58)

A renderer ended for hanging in its boot had lived the whole allowance, so
it restarted at once, forever; one whose boot never answered now counts
young. Only a renderer that started and answered its start hands what it
holds to the next, so a refusal loop keeps no ended links. A start that
throws is said rather than ending the daemon. A line heard after a link's
end performs no reach, so a late watch or hold cannot leak. Ids of an ended
renderer fail as down again, as the supervisor's to say. Both processes'
memory reports are taken at one moment. The renderer's file adapters are
built in one place. Comments and the design doc say what the code does:
the digest boot, the charge on Linux, storage refused in the renderer's
boot, and inputs landing between a request's two turns.
